title: Isomorphisms descend along etale surjections
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of bounded
constructible complexes on $X$. If $Lu^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism,
then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: At the fixed coefficient ring A, form the singleton family indexed by PUnit whose only arrow is f. Its joint surjectivity is exactly Surjective f. Its etaleness gives membership in the etale precoverage, and [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover], implemented by Scheme.etalePrecoverage_le_proetalePrecoverage, gives membership in the pro-etale precoverage. This includes the empty-scheme case without a nonemptiness hypothesis.

For sheaves with values in ModuleCat (ULift A), use the existing source theorem ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction (WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/FiniteCoefficient/LowerShriek/Open/Conservative.lean). It is the sheaf-axiom detection part of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: on every site object the base-changed covering detects injectivity and glues the unique local inverse. The published natural isomorphism ProEtale.upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction identifies actual inverse image with that localization restriction, the mechanism of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. NatIso.isIso_map_iff transfers invertibility to restriction. Applying the source detection theorem to the singleton cover proves that fixed-scalar inverse image reflects isomorphisms. This is the private proved helper fixedPullback_reflectsIsomorphisms; no new assumption or theorem hole is introduced.

Set A=P.Ring, with its existing finite-coefficient finiteness instance from [def-pur-conventions]. The exact intrinsic inverse image F underlying [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is definitionally the composite of the inverse canonical module realization equivalence, fixed-scalar upperStar, and the canonical realization equivalence on U. Each equivalence reflects isomorphisms, as does upperStar by the preceding step, so F reflects isomorphisms. The derived pullback in the hypothesis is definitionally F.mapDerivedCategory.

For every integer n, apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], namely F.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso n, to phi.hom. NatIso.isIso_map_iff and the pullback-isomorphism hypothesis show that F applied to H^n(phi.hom) is invertible. Reflection by F makes H^n(phi.hom) invertible. The natural comparison is on the derived category itself, so it already includes compatibility with inverted quasi-isomorphisms.

Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_iff, [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], to conclude that phi.hom is invertible in the ambient derived category. The inclusion of the full subcategory [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] reflects isomorphisms, so phi itself is invertible.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement and its finite pro-etale coefficient scope. Expanded the proof into the covering criterion, an explicit graph computation identifying inverse image with exact slice restriction, natural cohomology comparison, the sheaf-axiom local inverse, and the derived cohomology criterion. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes, no attachments. Avoided applying etale geometric-stalk conservativity to arbitrary pro-etale sheaves. Replaced irrelevant smooth-morphism statement dependency with the actual etale, surjective, separated, finite-type and coefficient definitions; recorded real Mathlib searches.

The current main-20261015 sk-prop-cohsm proof, first paragraph, explicitly uses that coordinate charts form a pro-etale covering; steps 1 and 4 spell out this detection. The historical unit sk-prop-cohsm steps 0, 3 and 4 local-to-global role is unchanged. No key unit statement is being realized by this auxiliary lemma; no unit fields changed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-Codex-Q33-c6f9a7524 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS for Q33/lem-pur-etale-iso-descent. The statement is unchanged and matches both blueprint snapshots exactly. Coefficients are A=A_{E,n} on X_proet (scope from def-pur-conventions), D^b_c is the full subcategory from def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, and Lu^* is the finite-level pullback from def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. The stmt_deps changes are justified: smooth morphisms are dropped, and separated comes from def-weil-proper-morphism. The delivery has no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and the graph is acyclic. Step 1: étale implies weakly étale (det-pe (1), Stacks 094X(4)) and the map is open (UniversallyOpen.of_flat, 01UA); with quasi-compactness of V this is exactly the condition in Stacks 0989 (proetale.tex:2126). Step 2: I checked that the graph pair (W,γ) is initial in I_W, because pr_U∘φ is the structure map, so the colimit is F(W). Inverse image is therefore restriction, and that restriction is exact by lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. Step 3: termwise representability is stated in the pullback definition, and homologyFunctorIso gives the natural comparison. Step 4 is an elementary sheaf-axiom gluing argument, complete and covering X=∅. Step 5: DerivedCategory.isIso_iff (HomologySequence.lean:88) plus fullness of D^b_c. The proof departs from the blueprint's geometric-stalk argument, and the departure is justified: lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative (4) shows stalk non-conservativity, and its cover-locality clause (1) is a generalization only in the different Λ_{T,Proet} category, so it is not cited and same_as stays []. I accept the three declared tool uses: det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization and lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. No SGA source is cited. No fixes were needed.
